method: For validation I used the whole-identifier congruence test: extend the 3,7,1 weight cycle one position rightward so the check digit itself receives weight 1, the rightmost payload digit weight 3, then 7, 1, 3, 7, 1 continuing leftward (weight is 3 when position p from the right, with p=0 at the check digit, satisfies p mod 3 = 1; 7 when p mod 3 = 2; 1 when p mod 3 = 0). I summed digit x weight over ALL digits including the check digit to get T, and declared the identifier VALID iff T mod 10 = 0. For computation I assigned weights left to right starting from the weight of position L (the payload length) counted from the right — for these 6-digit payloads L mod 3 = 0 so the leftmost digit gets weight 1 and the left-to-right weights are 1, 7, 3, 1, 7, 3, ending with weight 3 on the rightmost digit. I summed digit x weight to get S and found the check digit c by testing candidates 0-9 for the unique c with (S + c) mod 10 = 0. Every sum was computed digit by digit twice before recording.

derivations.compute:479812: L=6, 6 mod 3 = 0 so leftmost weight is 1; weights L-to-R 1,7,3,1,7,3: 4x1=4, 7x7=49, 9x3=27, 8x1=8, 1x7=7, 2x3=6; S = 4+49+27+8+7+6 = 101; need (101+c) mod 10 = 0; testing c=0..9, only c=9 gives 110 = 0 mod 10 -> c = 9
